newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates up a touch but still pressured.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates up a touch but still pressured.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates edged up from Wednesday's lows in routine Thursday trade, but were seen staying under pressure until the new credit quota kicks in on Friday.

Call money was quoted at bid prices of 1.50 to 1.81 percent, but dealers said the majority of deals had been done at 1.75 percent. On Wednesday, one-day money dipped to 1.25 percent in late afternoon trade.
Dealers said the low call rates reflected an ample special advances allocation on top of the expiring secured loans pact.
Call rates usually tend to fall towards the end of a pact, as players use up the savings accumulated over the three months.
But market liquidity was so ample yesterday that savings under the pact actually increased, a dealer said.
But dealers said the new credit quota, due to take effect on Friday along with a new 14-day cash reserve requirement, would bring rates back into line.

A new special advances pact due to be announced at 1500 GMT would hold the rate unchanged at 2.50 percent, they added. "The Dutch central bank will hold the rate steady despite speculation about a cut in Germany's (equivalent) repo rate," one said.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said Thursday the German central bank could not afford to ignore the economic signal represented by last week's record German jobless figures.
Several Dutch players interpreted this as presaging a possible near-term cut in Germany's repo rate. "But even if Germany does cut, we won't follow," a dealer said.

The guilder was quoted a touch softer against the mark at 112.34 per 100 marks from Wednesday's 112.315 fixing. The Dutch currency was also down against sterling at Wednesday's fixing at 3.00 guilders to the pound.
